newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Wheat keen to win Pakistan business.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Wheat keen to win Pakistan business.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Thursday it would compete vigorously against the United States in Pakistan wheat tenders.

"We've been invited to tender... for the January cargo and we will be submitting a price and hopefully it will be competitive," Mark Emons, AWB regional manager of international marketing, told Reuters.
"Our aim here is to sell Australian wheat and if that beats American wheat that's what we'll be doing," Emons said.

The Pakistani Ministry of Food and Agriculture has invited bids later this month for the supply of 270,000 tonnes U.S. Grade-2 or better soft white wheat to be financed under an export credit guarantee programme.
The AWB, through commodities trader Cargill, beat the U.S. in a December tender to deliver 225,000 tonnes of Australian white milling wheat, in the first tender to be lost by the U.S. this year.
The AWB's Emons said subsequent remarks by U.S. Agricultural Attache Maurice House in Pakistan that Australia engaged in trade-distorting practices were "a little unfortunate" and misguided.
"Mr House for some reason believes that the Pakistan government isn't allowed to make their own mind up when it comes to who is supplying the wheat," Emons said.
"It was a fair and open tender... we gave prices to everbody who asked for prices and tendered on that basis."
Pakistan bought 225,000 tonnes of Australian wheat from Cargill at about US$152 per tonne for December 11-31 shipment at its December 1 tender.
Australian trade commissioner Don Cairns on Wednesday said bids had been submitted by traders, not by the AWB.
Emons said that while Australia intends to be aggressive in its tendering, it would be impossible to sell all its exportable wheat this year, given expectations of a bumper crop of 21 million tonnes.
"We have limitations in total by what we can put through the system and export each month," he said.
"That's something we will be testing the limits on... we will not be able to sell all the tonnage that is grown this year."
Australian exports for December are nearing record levels, Emons said.
